text:
Matias Maccelli has fit quickly on Long Island. In his first 15 games as an Islander, after a season in Toronto, he has 2 goals and 11 points, 4 on the power play, and the Islanders win 58.1% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five when he's out there, about eight points better than without him.

This is who he is: a passer. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 92nd percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, with 20% of his setups going across the royal road, the pass that moves a goalie side to side, against 7% for a typical forward. Our closest comparison is Claude Giroux.

His 2.97 points per 60 sit above our talent range of 1.94 to 2.81, so expect some cooling, and reporter Stefen Rosner caught both sides of his game on Nov. 25, a slick backhand look and a lost one-on-one that let Toropchenko get behind him. The Islanders have won six of his last ten games. Our range puts him around 45 points by April.
headline: Maccelli is setting the table
